title: County of Ribagorza
capsule: The County of Ribagorza was a march county on the southern slopes of the Pyrenees, covering the valleys of the Ésera, Isábena, and Noguera Ribagorzana rivers, with its capital at Benabarre in what is now northeastern Aragon and adjacent Catalonia. It emerged as a distinct county in the later 9th century — traditionally traced to Raymond I (Ramón I) around 872 — and alternated between autonomy and the overlordship of Navarre and the County of Aragon. After Count Gonzalo died around 1045 the county was absorbed into the realm of his brother Ramiro I of Aragon, and thereafter served as a royal Aragonese appanage rather than an independent polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's territorial extent is imprecisely recorded; its Pyrenean borders shifted with local lordships and it lacked the administrative documentation of larger Iberian kingdoms.
